dataset.name: Five Years of Dissolved Oxygen, Temperature, Salinity, Depth, Weather Data from a Transitioning Wetland at Beaver Creek, Washington, USA
description: Groundwater dissolved oxygen (DO) variability in coastal system remains poorly understood despite its importance for biogeochemical cycling and ecosystem modeling. Here we investigate the temporal variability in groundwater DO and its hydro-climatic drivers across hourly to seasonal timescales in a transitioning wetland at Beaver Creek, Washington, USA. The site is transitioning from a freshwater forest to a brackish tidal wetland following removal of a barrier in 2014 that prevented tides from accessing the freshwater creek. By utilizing novel optical dissolved oxygen instrumentation (Opti O2, LLC) we obtained continuous, high-frequency (5-minute), in-situ measurements of DO from the flood-plain from June 26th, 2019 through September 30th, 2024. This 63 month dataset is comprised of groundwater dissolved oxygen, temperature, water level and salinity timeseries from the floodplain. This dataset also includes rainfall, air pressure, air temperature, and solar radiation data collected with a co-located Campbell ClimaVUE50 weather sensor. All data is contained within a single csv (2019-06-26 to 2024-09-30 Beaver Creek DO, saln, BGS, temp, weather.csv) that can easily be viewed either using software such as Excel or using any text editor.

measurementTechnique: A continuous time-series of temperature and DO, at ∆t = 5 min was obtained from the flood-plain well over a multi-year period. Opti O2 dissolved oxygen probe (www.optio2.com) equipped with internal thermistors was deployed in a slotted, screened well within the floodplain. Air temperature, pressure, rainfall and solar radiation data were collected with a Campbell ClimaVUE50 installed at the data logger located in the flood-plain. Depth and salinity data were collected using an In-Situ Aqua TROLL 200 installed in the well.

Opti O2 dissolved oxygen probes was initially installed in the river, seep and well on 2019-03-05. The Campbell ClimaVUE50 and well Aqua TROLL were installed on 2019-06-26. All data streams from the DO probe, Aqua TROLL and the ClimaVUE were autonomously telemetered to the cloud in quasi real-time (once an hour) from installation date to current. Reminder that this ESS-DIVE data repository only contains data collected from 2019-06-26 to 2024-09-30 for the well Opti O2 and Aquatroll probes, as well as the ClimaVUE data.
